items.note: This matches the reference's 02 hero closely. A full-bleed yolk band with a big sag arc holds a tight bold headline, a lead, and a blue pill next to a white on-field pill. A floating vignette of white cards, a ledge disc, a cloud and sparkles sits to the right, and the page then moves to cream cards with saturated pictogram covers. The vignette is looser than the reference's: it is a stack of near-identical white cards with stray dots, not one composed object like the phone and bubble in 01.

The centered headline, lead and stacked blue and white pills read well and match the reference's 04 phone hero. But the full-size vignette cards stack below the pills as their own column, so the yellow band runs about 1,400–1,600px. The first post appears only after two screens of yellow, while the reference keeps the phone band compact.

Same layout as light. The yolk hero sits on a navy page, the vignette cards turn indigo, and the post cards turn indigo with full-strength pictogram covers. It reads as a credible extension of the reference's night palette (03). The page still ends in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer.

The night version of the phone hero has the same stacking problem. The indigo vignette cards stack below the pills, the yolk band runs about two screens, and the content starts very late. The navy and indigo tones themselves are right.

Each sample opens with a compact header band that has a bold two-line title, meta, tags and a crescent-shaded block composition. Sample 1 uses a cream band beside a pink cover panel; samples 2 and 3 use green and yellow bands with a gentle arc. A reading column with a cream table-of-contents panel and cream quote and code blocks follows, all in the reference's warm-neutral, flat-tone language. Inline figure panels and related cards keep the pictogram kit.

The compact band has the title stacked large and a small shape cluster in the corner, close to the reference's 04 rhythm, and the cream table-of-contents and body follow. But the breadcrumb is squeezed beside the cluster. In sample 2 the link overlaps the truncated title. In sample 3 the link breaks word by word. The table-of-contents panel butts the arc's low point.

The night version keeps saturated green and yellow header bands, or an indigo band with a pink cover, over a navy page. Quotes, code and the table of contents sit in indigo panels, which reads like the reference's 03. The white footer bottom bar breaks the night page at the end.

The dark phone article has a compact hue band with the corner cluster, then indigo table-of-contents and quote panels, then readable body text on navy. It ends in the same bright white bottom bar. The breadcrumb crowding seen in light mode is here too.

The header bands are well built. Orange and yellow in samples 2 and 3 are full of flat, crescent-shaded document and shape scenes with a cloud and sparkles; sample 1 has a cream band with an orange cover. The body is cream-paneled like the reference. The weak spot is the mid-article figure in sample 1: white page cards with grey text lines, like a wireframe. It lacks the saturated flat-primitive drawing of the other samples and of the reference's 07.

The compact orange or yellow band (cream with a cover in sample 1) has a large stacked title and a corner cluster, followed by a cream table-of-contents and body. The rhythm is close to the reference's phone, but the breadcrumb again collides with the cluster: overlapping in sample 2, wrapping word by word in sample 3.

The orange and yellow bands keep full strength on the navy page, and the code, quote and figure panels turn indigo. It is a convincing derived night look. The bright white footer bottom bar is the only light surface on the page.
The night phone article is well layered: a hue band with a corner cluster, then indigo panels, with tags and pills readable on navy. It ends in the same white bottom bar.

A blue header band holds a big flat book-and-pencil scene with a cloud, sun and sparkles. The scene is well drawn, but the band is about 440px tall while the title and one line of text sit in its top-left corner. Half the band is empty blue. Below it come a spot-plate section title, prose and cream author cards with initials discs. The reference keeps tall bands for full hero text blocks (02).

Here the compact blue band works as the reference's phone band does: a large two-line title, a lead, an optional white pill and a small book cluster in the corner. Below it come spot-plate section headings, readable prose, cream author cards with colored initials discs, and a cream footer with a rise arc and an ink pill.
The night version has the same oversized blue header band with its title in the corner and empty left half. Indigo author cards on navy are fine, and the page again ends in a white bottom bar.
The compact blue band with a corner cluster, the indigo author cards and the white on-field pills hold the night palette well. The footer ends in a bright white bottom bar.

findings.summary: On phones, the front-page hero stacks its full-size vignette (three or four white cards plus shapes) as a column below the pills. The yolk band grows to about 1,400–1,600px, and the first post starts two screens down. The reference's phone hero is a compact band of headline, lead and pill, with art kept small or at the edge (04). This was named in the earlier rc.4 review and is still open.
findings.promptFix: Below `breakpoint.md`, a hero's vignette or composition is decoration and must not grow the band. Keep the band to its headline, lead and pills plus `space.8` and the arc, about one screen at most. Either cut the vignette to one piece of at most 140px tucked beside or under the pills, or drop it and keep two or three confetti shapes. Never stack more than one vignette card on a phone.

findings.summary: On desktop, the about page's header band takes its height from the art (about 440px) but holds only an h2 title and one line in the top-left corner. Half the band is empty colour, and the content starts near the bottom of the first screen. In the reference, a tall band is earned by a full text block (02). This repeats the open rc.4 gap and is still produced by the band's art-derived min-height.
findings.promptFix: Size a compact header band by its text, not its art. Drop the art-derived min-height: the band is its text block plus `space.10` above and `space.8` below, about 200–260px on desktop and never more than a third of the first screen. Cap the art box at the band's height and let it spread sideways with a wide viewBox. Only a front-page hero with a display headline, lead and pills may grow tall around its art.
findings.specRule: .ms-field--header { --ms-arc: var(--size-arc-sm); padding-block: var(--space-10) var(--space-8); min-height: calc(min(42vw, var(--size-band-art)) * 0.6 + var(--space-12)); }

findings.summary: In dark mode, every blog page ends in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer. It is the only light surface on a night page, while the reference's night palette stays dark to the edge (03). This is still open from rc.3 and rc.4.
findings.promptFix: Give the footer bottom bar its own role token, the darkest surface in both appearances: ink by day, and a step darker than the navy page at night, with white text. Keep `surface.inverse` for small floating pieces such as toasts.
findings.specRule: Footer | Cream band with rise arc, link columns, a signup field + ink pill; `surface.inverse` bottom bar with round icon buttons … (dark) `color.surface.inverse` | `#ffffff`

findings.summary: On phone article headers, the breadcrumb is squeezed beside the corner shape cluster. In one sample the parent link overlaps the truncated current-page label; in another the parent link wraps word by word.

In one sample, an in-article figure is drawn as white page cards with grey text lines and a lone dot, which looks like a wireframe. The other samples and the reference draw the same idea in saturated, crescent-shaded flat primitives (07).
